saints.name: St. Juan Diego Cuauhtlatoatzin
saints.title: Layman and Seer of Guadalupe
saints.shortBlurb: The humble Indian convert of Mexico to whom the Virgin of Guadalupe appeared, leaving her image upon his cloak…
biography: Juan Diego Cuauhtlatoatzin was a native of Mexico, baptized in his middle years by the first Franciscan missionaries. In December of 1531, on the hill of Tepeyac near Mexico City, the Blessed Virgin Mary appeared to him as a native woman and asked that a church be built there; when the bishop sought a sign, she filled his cloak with roses out of season, and on the cloak was found imprinted the image of Our Lady of Guadalupe.
Juan Diego spent his remaining years in prayer near the shrine, telling all who came of the Lady's message. His witness and the miraculous image drew millions of the native peoples to the faith.
saints.knownFor: The seer of Our Lady of Guadalupe, whose tilma bears her image.
patronage: the indigenous peoples of the Americas
